Recall that if $A$ is a $4\times 4$ real matrix that has complex eigenvalues 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{4}$ 

with corresponding eigenvectors 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2}\,$ and $\,{v}_{3}={\overset{―}{v}}_{4},$ 

then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{3}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{3})\end{aligned}]
$$

and

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & \text{Re}({v}_{3}) & \text{Im}({v}_{3}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third and forth columns of $P$ correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{3}.$ Therefore,

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -1 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
